R130.note: Replaces cmd.exe /C batch with separate exec.Command calls per tool using argument arrays, plus a hostname/IP-shaped allowlist matching what ping/nslookup expect; drops the original's && short-circuit and per-command error surfacing but this is disclosed in code comments and does not reject legitimate targets.

R131.note: Clean argument-array exec.Command replacing sh -c string concatenation; matches the stated contract exactly with no other observable change.

R132.note: Rejects rooted paths and '..', then verifies the resolved path stays under the reports root via Path.GetFullPath/StartsWith; closes the Path.Combine override without restricting legitimate relative filenames.

R133.note: Uses mongoose's own sanitizeFilter() API, the documented non-rejecting fix for operator injection; wraps $-prefixed nested values in $eq rather than denying requests, preserving legitimate scalar extra-criteria and the ownerId/_id fields.

R134.note: Reorders to resolve-then-normalize and adds a startsWith containment check, correctly rejecting escapes per the stated contract; the write-up's explanation that Path.resolve() treats an absolute string argument as 'relative' is factually backwards (resolve() returns the absolute argument verbatim per the Path.resolve(String) contract), though the subsequent startsWith check still catches and rejects it in practice, so the code is correct despite the wrong reasoning.

R135.note: Allowlist maps the finite, documented set of diagnostic tool names to fixed absolute paths, appropriate since 'tool' is meant to be one of a handful of known utilities; the unvalidated 'target' argument is unchanged from the original and is outside this specific finding's reported sink (the tainted executable name).

R136.note: Adds the separator-aware containment check (full == base || HasPrefix(full, base+separator)) that precisely closes the sibling-directory prefix bypass with no other behavior change.

R137.note: Verified by compiling and running against real commons-jexl3 3.3: sandbox.white(ReportRow.class.getName()) with no execute()/read() permissions added denies ALL method/property access on ReportRow through JEXL (row.getRegion()=='EMEA' silently returns false instead of throwing, row.amount throws 'undefined property') - the opposite of the write-up's claim that it 'allows access to...ReportRow getters'; also a denylist of five named classes is a weaker containment shape for a code-execution sink than a true allowlist.

R138.note: Adds an ownership-scoped repository query (findByIdAndCustomerUsername) using the caller's identity from SecurityContextHolder, closing the missing check without altering behavior for legitimate owners.

R139.note: Ad hoc scalar-only check on extraCriteria blocks the specific operator-injection example but is the wrong shape for this sink versus mongoose's own sanitizeFilter(); it adds a new 400 rejection for any nested/array extra-criteria value not present in the original code, stated in the write-up but not called for by any stated contract.

R140.note: Replaces filename-derived probeContentType with Apache Tika content-byte detection and derives the stored extension from the detected type rather than client input; the added extension is disclosed and does not reject legitimate uploads.

R141.note: Argument-array subprocess.run without shell=True closes the shell metacharacter vector for the reported sink and preserves the conversion behavior/return value unchanged.

R142.note: Switches to mysql2's execute() with a ? placeholder, the standard parameterized-query fix, returning identical results for legitimate userId values.
